title: Maximal tori inside Borels and conjugacy of maximal tori
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A maximal torus is a torus subgroup maximal under inclusion. A group is solvable if its successive scheme-theoretic derived subgroups eventually become trivial, where the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup. Let $G$ be smooth and connected. Every Borel subgroup $B\subseteq G$ contains a torus that is maximal in $G$. For any two maximal tori $T_1,T_2\subseteq G$, there is $g\in G(F)$ with $gT_1g^{-1}=T_2$ as subgroup schemes. Equality of conjugate subgroups means equality after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. No reductivity hypothesis is imposed; the rank-zero torus is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354--355; paragraph following Definition 17.12, printed p.355; solvable case Theorem 16.33(d), printed pp.336--337.

proof.text: Choose maximal subgroups by dimension. Every torus is smooth and connected by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus], and is solvable because it is commutative. The dimension bound and strict-inclusion assertion of [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] show that every torus lies in a maximal torus: among the tori containing it choose one of greatest dimension. The rank-zero torus makes this set nonempty. The same greatest-dimension argument among smooth connected solvable subgroups containing a given torus gives a Borel containing it. In particular Borels and ambient maximal tori exist.

source.place: Definition 17.6 and the paragraph before Example 17.7, printed pp.353--354; proof of Theorem 17.10 and paragraph following Definition 17.12, printed p.355.

proof.text: Let B and C be Borels. Form X=G/B using [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. Its fppf coset description defines left translation by G: (h,gB) maps to hgB; this is well-defined on cosets, commutes with base change, and hence defines the action on the represented quotient. The identity coset makes X nonempty. The map q:G to X is a quotient in the sense required by [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry]: it is faithfully flat and of finite type over F, hence of finite presentation; the isomorphism G x_F B = G x_X G says that two T-points have the same image exactly when their ratio lies in B; and every T-point of X lifts fppf, hence fpqc, locally because X represents the fppf sheaf quotient. By [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry], X is proper and of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] to C acting on X. It gives an F-point x fixed by C after every F-algebra extension. Lift x to g in G(F) using [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. For every F-algebra A and c in C(A), fixedness says cgB=gB, so the coset-fibre assertion gives g^{-1}cg in B(A). Thus g^{-1}Cg is a closed smooth connected solvable subgroup of B, and maximality of the Borel g^{-1}Cg forces equality with B. Consequently C=gBg^{-1} as subgroup schemes.

source.place: Theorem 17.9(b), proof, printed p.354; quotient action in Definition 5.20, printed p.104.

proof.text: Establish the solvable case with its actual section argument. Let H be smooth, connected and solvable, and let S_1,S_2 be maximal tori of H. By [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup] the derived subgroup of a smooth connected group is a normal smooth connected closed subgroup; iterating, each term of the derived series of H is smooth and connected and normal in its predecessor. Each quotient D^iH/D^{i+1}H is commutative, since the commutator morphism of D^iH factors through D^{i+1}H, so the presheaf quotients and their fppf sheafifications are commutative. Thus the derived series is a finite closed-subgroup normal series with commutative fppf quotients, so [lem-sfb-lie-kolchin-triangular-embedding] applies and identifies H with J inside B_n. By [lem-sfb-triangular-diagonal-kernel], V=J intersect U_n is smooth connected normal unipotent, D=J/V is smooth and connected and embeds as a closed subgroup of (G_m)^n. Hence D is a torus by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus]. Apply [lem-sfb-solvable-torus-complements] to H=J, U=V: each q|_{S_i}:S_i to D is an isomorphism. The composites s_i:D to S_i to J using its inverse are group-scheme sections of q. Since D is smooth, [lem-sfb-triangular-quotient-section-conjugacy] supplies v in V(F) with s_2=Int(v) composed with s_1. Their images are S_2 and vS_1v^{-1}, so S_2=vS_1v^{-1}. This equality is on every F-algebra, as is the cited section equality.

source.place: Theorem 16.33(d), printed p.336; Theorems 16.26--16.27, printed pp.332--333; Summary 16.29(b), printed p.334.

proof.text: Let T_1,T_2 be maximal tori of G. By step 1 choose Borels B_1,B_2 containing them. Step 2 gives g in G(F) such that gB_1g^{-1}=B_2. The tori gT_1g^{-1} and T_2 are maximal in B_2: a larger torus in B_2 would be a larger torus in G (after conjugating back for T_1). Apply the solvable case of step 3 to B_2 to obtain b in B_2(F) with b(gT_1g^{-1})b^{-1}=T_2. Then h=bg satisfies hT_1h^{-1}=T_2. The calculation holds on A-points for every commutative F-algebra A, so it is the required equality of closed subgroup schemes.

Finally fix any Borel B. By step 1 choose an ambient maximal torus T and a Borel B_0 containing T. Step 2 supplies g in G(F) with gB_0g^{-1}=B. Therefore gTg^{-1} is a torus contained in B. It is maximal in G, since conjugating any larger torus back by g^{-1} would contradict maximality of T. Both conclusions are preserved when the maximal torus has rank zero, and no step used reductivity.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 17.10 and paragraph following Definition 17.12, printed pp.354--355, with the solvable case expanded through Theorem 16.33(d), printed p.336.
